subject: MedSync — inference economics & feature pricing alignment

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MedSync — inference economics & feature pricing alignment

Hi Claire — thanks again for a productive demo call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (from our notes)
- Primary use: patient intake summarization + eligibility suggestions for care coordinators (short-form generation + classification).
- Target users: 1,200 active users initially, ~45k messages/month (~12M tokens/month estimated).
- Critical non-functional asks: sub-200ms tail latency on chat endpoints (p95), SOC2 compliance, and region US-WEST.
- Budget band (your comment): mid-five-figures / month (you mentioned "flexible but need to stay inside procurement guardrails").

Open qualification items for us to confirm
1) Can you confirm the 12M token/month estimate (or provide high/low scenarios)?
2) Preferred procurement timeline (contract by end of Sep / pilot in Sep?)
3) Target CAC payback window for this feature (months) and target margin percent on product line (helps pick quantization/throughput trade-offs).

What we’re sending you now
- Attached: high-level pricing summary (redwood_pricing_summary.xlsx) with two starter tiers: "Pilot" and "Scale". Each tier includes recommended batching and quantization knobs for cost targets.
- Shared Drive: demo recording and feature brief (link below).

Suggested near-term next steps
- You: confirm token scenarios and procurement contact (I added Procurement on this thread).
- Us: build a short $/1M token model and a $/feature sketch tied to your 12M estimate; we’ll include CAC-payback scenarios (1, 6, 12 months).
- Schedule: aiming for a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the model.

If you prefer, we can produce two quick options: (A) cost-optimized (lower $/1M tokens, higher latency variability) and (B) SLA-backed (higher $/1M tokens, strict p95). Which would you prefer we prioritize?

Thanks — talk soon.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Aditya — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming the high-level numbers from our side: 

- Token volume: baseline 8–12M tokens/mo (best case 15M with adoption), please model low/expected/high.
- Budget: target $45k–$90k / month (we are early-stage but want a 6–12 month runway for pilots).
- CAC payback: our finance asks for 9–12 month payback on feature-led acquisition; product would accept 6–9 if net margin holds.
- $/feature: ideally under $0.50 incremental cost per completed patient summary at scale (this drives our willingness to expand).

Procurement note: procurement@medsync.ai is our gate for any contract language. They’ll ask for SOC2, data residency info, and an SOW outlining milestones for pilot and measurement of success. I’ve attached the internal feature brief for context (medsync_feature_brief.pdf).

Next steps for us: please share the $/1M token breakdown and two scenarios you mentioned (cost-optimized vs SLA-backed). We’re available for a 30-min sync on Wed 8/11 morning PST.

—Claire
Claire Ng
Head of Product, MedSync Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MedSync — inference economics & feature pricing alignment

Internal note / modeling assumptions for the follow-up (keeping this short):

Key inputs from Claire: 8–15M tokens/mo, target $45k–$90k/mo, CAC payback 6–12m, target ~$0.50/feature.

High-level cost model (back-of-envelope) — inputs we should use for the deck: 
- Inference engine cost assumptions: base hosted price before margin: $10 / 1M tokens (cost to Redwood at Pilot config), optimized exec: $6 / 1M tokens (with quantization + batching).
- Two commercial proposals to put forward:
  * Pilot (SLA best-effort): $18 / 1M tokens, includes 99th percentile guidance but no hard SLA, expected margin ~45% at baseline 12M tokens.
  * Enterprise (SLA-backed): $30 / 1M tokens, includes p95/p99 SLOs, 24/7 support, prioritized capacity; expected margin ~60% at 12M tokens.
- $/feature mapping: assume average 800 tokens per completed summary (prompt + response + metadata).
  * Pilot: 800 tokens => ~0.0144 $/feature @ $18/1M => $0.0144? Wait compute: (800 tokens / 1,000,000) * $18 = $0.0144 per feature — that’s far below $0.50, so Claire's target looks conservative (good).
  * Enterprise: (800 / 1,000,000) * $30 = $0.024 per feature.
- CAC payback modeling: if they want 9 months payback and target contribution margin 40%, we can map to how many paying seats / ARPU to justify price. We should build a simple waterfall: tokens -> $/1M -> margin -> CAC payback months.

Action items I’ll take before Wed sync:
- Build a 1-sheet XLS with 3 volume scenarios and the two pricing tiers, showing $/feature, monthly cost, gross margin at Redwood, and CAC payback buckets (1, 6, 9, 12 months).
- Flag any compliance/region cost adders (e.g., private-region hosting adds ~10% on top).

Notes to Aditya/Karthik: avoid overselling the unit price ranges; present a clear pilot path with an upgrade to SLA-backed pricing once usage is proven. Will have the XLS and a 2-slide summary by EOD Tue.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
